subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Lesson 5: Vocabulary and Grammar – Animal verbs; First conditional
outcomes: Name and use animal verbs like roar, sting, dive and curl up.
Make first conditional sentences: If + present, will + verb.
Talk about real things that can happen in the future.

tf.why: Yes, roar is the loud sound a lion makes.

tf.s: A hedgehog curls up to make itself into a ball.
tf.why: Yes, it curls up to stay safe.
Yes, a bee stings with the end of its body.

tf.s: In the first conditional, we use will in the if part.
tf.why: The if part uses the present simple: If it rains, …

tf.s: The negative of will is won't.
Dig means to fly high in the sky.
tf.why: Dig means to make a hole in the ground.

tf.s: If we plant more flowers, more bees will come.
tf.why: Yes, this sentence is correct: present + will.

tf.s: If I will see a lion, I will run away.
tf.why: Say: If I see a lion, I'll run away.

tf.s: The first conditional talks about things that can really happen in the future.
tf.why: Yes, it is for real future possibilities.

tf.s: Hide means to show yourself so everyone can see you.
tf.why: Hide means to go where others can't see you.

boxes.q: A hedgehog makes itself into a ball. It …
boxes.why: Curl up means make your body into a ball.

boxes.q: Complete: If you come with us, you ___ with the best animals.
boxes.why: The result part uses will + verb.
Rabbits dig holes in the ground.

boxes.q: Complete: If you ___ (not hurry), you'll miss the bus.
boxes.why: The if part uses the present simple.

boxes.q: Which verb? A scorpion can ___ you.
boxes.why: A scorpion stings with its tail.

boxes.q: Which animal dives into the water?
Complete: If you shout, the gazelles will ___.
Choose: If you look up, you ___ an eagle.
boxes.why: Use will + verb after the if part.

boxes.q: What tense is in the if part of a first conditional?

mcq.q: Which verb means 'go away quickly on foot because you are scared'?
mcq.why: Run away is on foot; fly away is with wings.

mcq.q: What is the correct form of the first conditional?
mcq.why: The if part is present; the result uses will.

mcq.q: Which animal verb means 'cut into something with your teeth'?

mcq.why: Lions are famous for their loud roar.

mcq.q: Complete: If a scorpion ___ you, you'll need to go to hospital.
mcq.why: After if, use the present simple: stings.

mcq.q: Make it negative: If I join the lions, the birds will be happy.
o: If I join the lions, the birds won't be happy.
If I don't join the lions, the birds will be happy.
If I join the lions, the birds don't will be happy.
If I won't join the lions, the birds will be happy.
mcq.why: We change will to won't in the result part.

o: If you touch a hedgehog, it will curl up.
If you will touch a hedgehog, it curls up.
If you will touch a hedgehog, it will curl up.
If you touched a hedgehog, it will curl up.
mcq.why: Present in the if part, will in the result.

mcq.q: Your class wants more birds in the school garden. Which plan uses the first conditional correctly?
o: If we put food out, more birds will come.
If we will put food out, more birds come.
If we put food out, more birds came.
If we putting food out, more birds will come.
mcq.why: Good! Present simple, then will + verb.

mcq.q: Which is the best advice if you see a scorpion?
o: If you see a scorpion, move away slowly.
If you see a scorpion, touch it.
If you see a scorpion, pick it up.
If you see a scorpion, sit next to it.
mcq.why: Moving away slowly keeps you safe.

mcq.q: In a conditional chain, what comes next? If it rains, I'll stay home. If I stay home, …
mcq.why: Each result starts the next if sentence.
